name: Nadia Haddad (synthetic)

facts.label: use software libraries
facts.story: Builds the booking screens from React components and a handful of well-chosen libraries.

facts.label: use software design patterns
facts.story: Structures form components so that labels, errors and focus handling are written once and reused.

facts.label: debug software
facts.story: Reproduces reported interface bugs with a screen reader and fixes them with a test that fails first.

facts.label: design user interface
facts.story: Turns the designer's drawings into working screens and checks them against the drawing together with her.

facts.label: JavaScript Framework
facts.story: Builds the booking screens in React and keeps the components usable with keyboard and screen reader.

answers.recent_work: I finished my degree here a year ago, and since then I've been a front-end developer at a software company that makes tools for logistics. I build the screens in React and TypeScript, and I sit with a designer to check that they work as drawn. I have dyslexia, so I've got a habit of building checks into everything I do, which is probably why I like writing tests.
answers.example: A customer complained that the booking form was impossible to use with a screen reader. I went through it with a screen reader myself and found that the error messages were not announced and the date picker trapped the keyboard. I rebuilt the date field with proper labels and focus handling, and wrote tests for it. The customer's accessibility audit passed on the next round.
answers.tools: React and TypeScript, mostly. Figma to read the designs. Jest and Testing Library for tests, and Playwright for a few full flows. For accessibility I use a screen reader and the browser's audit tools. Git, of course, and code review every day.
answers.people: A team of six: three developers, a designer, a tester and a product owner. I work most closely with the designer, and the product owner brings customer feedback to me directly. I'm the one who usually looks at accessibility in the team, since I raised it in the first place.
answers.beyond: During my studies I did a course project on design systems, and I still maintain a small open source component library that I started there. I also tutored first-year students in programming for two semesters.
answers.open_floor: I'd like it noted that I write documentation for what I build. People in the team say the component docs are what they actually open.
answers.looking_for: Front-end or full-stack work, ideally in a product company, with some design collaboration. English is fine for work and I'm studying Finnish in the evenings; I can already follow meetings. Hybrid or remote, available right away.

probes: For the design system I built a button, a text field and a modal, each with documented keyboard behaviour. The modal was the hard one: focus has to stay inside it and go back to the trigger when it closes. I tested it by tabbing through it until nothing escaped.

Last month a colleague's pull request changed a colour that dropped the contrast under the accessibility guideline. I caught it by checking the contrast ratio in review, and we picked a darker shade together.
